title: Co-doped Bi2Te3: dilute impurity exchange and ordering temperatures

decision_points.kind: estimator / competing explanation (mean-field vs percolation-limited order)
decision_points.fork: How to turn the archived impurity exchange into an ordering temperature at 5% + 5% doping
decision_points.wrong_choice: Mean field: the two-sublattice estimate k_B T = (1/3) lambda_max(c_b J0_ab), or the authors' averaged (T_AA + T_BB + T_AB)/3 times the concentration
decision_points.consequence: T_C three- to eightfold too high (two-sublattice MF 60-82 K and authors' rule 22-39 K against 11-20 K for the ordered compositions; 33 K or 16 K for V2Cr2, which does not order above 0.8 K); Nb ranked best

decision_points.kind: disorder averaging (the scatter is visible only across random placements)
decision_points.fork: How many random dopant placements to average before comparing sizes
decision_points.wrong_choice: One random placement per supercell size (a single disorder realization), as in a clean-crystal finite-size analysis
decision_points.consequence: Sample-to-sample scatter dominates: for single placements the L = 3/4 crossing is missing or off by > 20% in 72% (V5Cr5) and 34% (Cr5Mo5, Cr5Mn5) of cases; the first placements give 14.9 K for V5Cr5 (+39%) and no crossing for Cr5Mn5

decision_points.kind: competing explanations (cross-species coupling strength vs frustration); discriminating calculation under budget
decision_points.fork: Which co-dopant raises the Curie temperature of Cr most
decision_points.wrong_choice: Rank by the largest cross-coupling / mean-field T_C (Nb: J0(Cr-Nb) = 257 meV, MF 97 K), as the paper's mean-field analysis suggests, without simulating each candidate
decision_points.consequence: Nb chosen; its antiferromagnetic Nb-Nb shells (6.10 and 7.51 A) frustrate the network, so Cr5Nb5 has at most weak, sample-dependent order (all estimates <= ~16 K), while Cr5Mo5 orders at ~20 K (Mo's 6.49 A antiferromagnetic shell has only 3 neighbours)

decision_points.kind: regime judgement (dilution below the percolation of strong couplings)
decision_points.wrong_choice: Scale T_C with concentration from 5% + 5% (or mean field, 33 K)
decision_points.consequence: A finite T_C of ~4 K is reported; the network of couplings strong enough to order above 2 K does not percolate (scaled m^2 falls with size down to 0.8 K)

decision_points.kind: evidence discovered in the purchased rows (missing calculations; collapsed run)
decision_points.fork: What to do with the Co-Co dimers, absent from the archive within 7.8 A (the 9.99 A run lost its moment)
decision_points.wrong_choice: Fill the missing Co-Co couplings with zeros (the authors' mean-field sums implicitly do this) and report a number
decision_points.consequence: A fabricated T_C for Cr5Co5; the data do not determine it (null)

decision_points.kind: convergence under a binding budget (exchange range)
decision_points.fork: Whether the far shells (7-16, 8.8-12.2 A, a separate purchase per pair) are needed
decision_points.wrong_choice: Buy only shells 0-6 (the strong couplings) to save budget
decision_points.consequence: T_C of the frustrated compositions shifts beyond the tolerance (see calibration: near_shells_only)

decision_points.kind: archive defect discovered in the rows (mislabelled column); competing explanation (moment collapse)
decision_points.fork: How to read the dimer moments m1/m2
decision_points.wrong_choice: Take m2 ~ 0.01 muB (shells 1-16) as collapse of impurity 2's moment in the dimer and drop that species (Mn, Mo in the Cr-X rows) from the spin model
decision_points.consequence: Cr5X5 reduces to Cr 5% alone (T_C ~3 K); m2 is impurity 2's moment only in the shell-0 cluster, the same species keeps its full moment as impurity 1 in its own rows

graded_fields: curie_temperature_K[V5Cr5], [Cr5Mo5], [Cr5Mn5] within 20% of the reference Monte Carlo T_C
curie_temperature_K[V2Cr2] <= 2 K (no order above 2 K; 0 expected)

length_estimate.catalog_size: 276 pair windows (210 + 66 units) plus unlimited Monte Carlo

runtime_dependencies: numpy/scipy (runtime image); the lab compiles its Monte Carlo kernel (mc_dilute.c, ~200 lines of C) with the image's gcc at build time; no extra packages

data_provenance.staged: all 2077 archived exchange rows (served per pair and shell window), CIF lines; the authors' mean-field Tc matrix and notebook are not staged

notes: Hidden values are consequences of the archived Hamiltonian (Monte Carlo with the lab's own code path on larger cells and more disorder samples), not archived numbers; the paper reports only mean-field estimates and leaves Monte Carlo to future work. T_C is graded because the exchange set and the estimator (thermodynamic-limit order of the stated classical model) are fixed; across sizes L = 3-6 the scaled-magnetization crossings agree to within 6-8%.

curie_temperature_K[V2Cr2].reference: no order above 0.8 K (scaled <m^2> falls with size at every T for L = 3/4/5; Binder ratio ~1.6)
curie_temperature_K[V2Cr2].tolerance: <= 3.0 K (0 = no order above 2 K; 1 K allowance for noise-level Binder crossings)

ablation_notes.near_shells_only: shells 0-6 only: no order in the probed ranges (scaled <m^2> falls with size at every T, Binder ratio ~1.65 down to 6 K for V5Cr5 and 10 K for Cr5Mo5), recorded as 0
ablation_notes.zero_filled_coco: missing Co-Co set to 0: no order above 2 K (scaled <m^2> falls with size); any number fails the null check
ablation_notes.dimer_moment_collapse: Mn/Mo dropped from the spin model: Cr 5% alone, reference T_C (L = 4/5 scaled crossing)
ablation_notes.single_placement_per_size: first random placement of the L = 3 and L = 4 reference sets only; 0 = no crossing

best_codopant_for_Cr.Nb_note: Nb value is the largest crossing + jackknife error over two independent reference sets (upper bound); Cr5Nb5 is not graded as a number
